item.title: Xi eyes BRICS' next 'golden decade'
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Xi eyes BRICS' next 'golden decade' He hails past 20 years of growth and vitality, calls for promoting innovation, peace and stability President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that China is ready to work with all parties to build consensus and usher in a third "golden decade" of BRICS cooperation, calling on the grouping to lead efforts to advance innovation, safeguard peace and stability, promote mutual learning among civilizations and improve global governance. Addressing Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the capital of India, Xi said China will assume the rotating presidency of BRICS next year and host the 19th summit. China previously hosted BRICS summits in 2011, 2017 and 2022. This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation, which emerged amid the collective rise of emerging markets and developing countries. Xi said solidarity and cooperation have remained the source of strength for BRICS throughout its two-decade journey. He urged members to treat one another with sincerity, seek common ground while respecting differences, and respect each other's core concerns. Members should deepen mutual understanding and properly manage differences through communication and dialogue to ensure the steady and long-term development of BRICS cooperation, he said. From its original four members, BRICS has grown into a family of 11 full members and 10 partner countries. Its members account for nearly half the world's population and over one-fourth of global trade. Xi said the grouping's historic expansion and comprehensive, multilevel cooperation framework have ushered in a new stage of high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation. With unilateralism and power politics undermining multilateralism and the international order, BRICS countries should stand firmly on the right side of history, steer the international order toward greater fairness and equity, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity, he said. On innovation-driven development, Xi welcomed BRICS countries' participation in the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, which was launched by China in July and is based in Shanghai, and proposed a BRICS initiative on using AI to advance new industrialization. On peace and stability, Xi noted that the situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid, and said China will work with fellow BRICS members to play a due role in bringing peace and tranquility to the Middle East and the Gulf region. Xi also called for greater mutual learning among civilizations through the BRICS people-to-people exchanges forum, the sharing of governance experience, and deeper cooperation in the areas of culture, tourism and education, including more exchanges among young people. On global governance, he urged support for the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core and called for opposition to all forms of protectionism. BRICS should help shape governance in emerging areas such as cyberspace, outer space and the deep sea, while strengthening the voice of the Global South, he said. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said BRICS has established a distinct identity on the global stage over the past 20 years by respecting different perspectives and moving forward through consensus. AI, cyberspace, outer space, biotechnology and critical technologies are shaping not only future opportunities, but also the rules that will govern the future, Modi said. "We must work to transform the Global South from rule-takers into rule-shapers," he said. The meeting participants highly commended the development achievements made by BRICS over the past two decades, saying that BRICS countries have a responsibility to speak out for the Global South, defend multilateralism and jointly address global challenges in the face of intensifying geopolitical conflicts and rising unilateralism. They said they appreciate China's important contribution to the development and expansion of the BRICS mechanism, and also support China in successfully hosting the 19th BRICS Summit during its presidency next year and working together to push BRICS cooperation to a new level. The summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration of the 18th BRICS Summit. China has been an important participant, builder and promoter of BRICS. Xi has, at different key stages, proposed a series of initiatives for the grouping's development. In 2014, he advocated the BRICS spirit of openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation. In 2017, he proposed the "BRICS Plus" cooperation approach, extending BRICS cooperation beyond its members to the broader Global South. In 2024, he called for a BRICS committed to peace, innovation, green development, justice and closer people-to-people exchanges. Lan Jianxue, director of the Department for Asia-Pacific Studies at the China Institute of International Studies, said these proposals have helped guide and broaden BRICS cooperation, extending it beyond economic ties into a more comprehensive framework. China could draw on its comprehensive industrial system, as well as BRICS' innovation and AI cooperation platforms, to share technologies, conduct joint research and provide training, Lan said. Such efforts could help partner countries develop digital industries and participate more fully in industrial and supply chains. Ayanda Holo, president of TV BRICS Africa, said he looks forward to covering next year's summit in China. Citing China's moves to offer zero-tariff access to African countries with which it has diplomatic relations, Holo said he hopes other BRICS members and partners could also gain greater access to the Chinese market and share in the opportunities created by China's development. During the meeting, leaders from BRICS countries also visited a photo exhibition, planted trees and posed for a group photo.

item.title: Alliance hails smart farming, rural growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Alliance hails smart farming, rural growth For Indian student Aarafat Chouhan, a visit to Qiantang district in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, offered a close look into how technology is improving rural life and agricultural practices. "Honestly, I was most excited to see smart farming and digital tech in action right here on the ground," he said. Chouhan is among dozens of international students who are members of the BRICS Youth Agricultural Development Promotion Alliance, which was officially launched in Qiantang in June. The alliance, comprised of 58 students from BRICS countries and partners, is focused on modern agriculture, rural governance and the integration of agriculture and tourism. The initiative is aimed at turning international students into observers and potential participants in rural development, granting them a firsthand experience in local agricultural projects and an opportunity to explore how China's rural vitalization practices can be replicated in other countries. Chouhan, a student at China Jiliang University in Hangzhou, highlighted how agriculture is deeply connected to people's lives and the economy in India, adding, however, that farmers continue to face significant challenges. "What really draws me to Qiantang is seeing how practical technology is put straight into the hands of everyday farmers," Chouhan said. "It's not just tech for the sake of tech, but actually improving real livelihoods. That's a model I really want to understand better." He is also interested in how the district is making rural areas more attractive to young entrepreneurs. It builds incubators, offers policy incentives and provides solid digital infrastructure so that starting an agricultural business actually makes financial sense, he said. According to local authorities, Qiantang has established 16 practice stations — for young people visiting rural areas for firsthand experiences — and cultivated 525 agricultural entrepreneurs. Chouhan said the approach has relevance for both China and India, where young people often move to big cities in search of employment. "Qiantang shows that if you modernize the countryside, young people will happily bring their talent back home," he added. For Zafarbek Abdullaev, an Uzbek student and member of the alliance, his interest is in how rural tourism drives local economies. "To be exact, I'm focused on how a normal farming village like Xinjiang (in Qiantang district) turns its land, its food, and its story into real income, and still keeps its young people at home," he said. He highlighted the role of young agricultural entrepreneurs who return to rural areas to start businesses, sell products online, develop brands and operate guesthouses. "Villages join together, share one brand, and bargain as a group. So one farmer does not stand alone against a big company. I believe this is the part most worth copying," he said. In Uzbekistan, rural communities have abundant cultural resources, traditional foods and handicrafts but are still struggling to find ways to generate more income locally, he said. The Qiantang fieldwork is being further supported by a rural vitalization competition among international students. As part of the competition, students from BRICS nations and countries involved in the Belt and Road Initiative are invited to conduct in-depth research into villages in Qiantang and document rural development through photographic, written and data works. "Being an observer is a great opportunity because it bridges the gap between theory and actual reality," Chouhan said. "It's one thing to read about rural development on paper, but using photos, videos, and real field data makes these lessons genuine and easy for other developing nations to learn from." Abdullaev said international students should go beyond simply describing China's achievements. "Our job is not to say 'China is amazing' and go home. It is to turn what we saw into something another country can actually use," he said. Teng Lingjian, chairman of the Hangzhou Qiantang Center for Contemporary Internationalization Studies, said agriculture provides common ground for cooperation among BRICS countries. "When international students take successful entrepreneurial experiences back to their countries, this kind of visible result is what makes technology sharing truly effective," Teng said. At the same time, the center plans to take a more proactive approach by sending its agricultural technologies, entrepreneurs and young talent to BRICS countries. "We hope to have deeper communication and cooperation with local agricultural projects and researchers," Teng said. The final goal is to address major issues of common concern among BRICS countries, such as food security, he added. Chen Ye in Hangzhou contributed to this story.

item.title: Ties with new hometown sealed
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Ties with new hometown sealed A chance encounter inspires a community to strengthen its bond with Keqiao Rolling up his sleeves and extending his arm to donate blood has become a familiar ritual for Neeraj Punhani. For 12 years, the 49-year-old Indian has regularly joined blood donation drives in Keqiao district of Shaoxing, Zhejiang province, where he has lived for 23 years while running a textile import business that exports products to India. It all began with a 12-year-old girl nicknamed Jia Jia. In December 2014, she was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Doctors said she would need blood transfusions and chemotherapy for a long time. The need for blood, coupled with mounting medical expenses, pushed her father, Wei Baoshi, who supported a family of five through odd jobs, to the brink of despair. On Dec 22, 2014, Punhani saw a post on the social media app WeChat saying Jia Jia was urgently in need of blood. Moved by a photo of the girl who had lost her hair during chemotherapy, he decided to help. "I wanted to help this girl. It touched my heart because my brothers and sisters and I all have daughters. So I felt like our own daughter needed help." The next morning, Punhani brought 16 fellow Indians and three Chinese friends to Hangzhou, capital of Zhejiang, to donate blood. On Jan 3, 2015, more than 100 Indians arrived at a blood donation center in Keqiao, with 96 donating a total of 33.8 liters of blood. More Indians who had been away on business returned to donate the following day. The support went further than blood donations. Two weeks later, Punhani and his Indian friends raised 160,000 yuan ($23,800) to help cover Jia Jia's medical expenses. The experience prompted Punhani to turn a one-time act of kindness into a long-running tradition. He began promoting voluntary blood donations through WeChat and posters at Indian companies, restaurants and other places frequented by Indians. The effort was also rooted in an earlier experience. On May 9, 2013, an Indian man who worked in Keqiao fell seriously ill and urgently needed blood plasma. The Zhejiang Blood Center and Shaoxing Central Blood Station organized a campaign under the theme "love without borders, blood continues life", in which 76 Chinese people donated blood for him. He later recovered. "I thought to myself at the time that I must find an opportunity to do something for this city," Punhani said. Since then, Punhani and his fellow Indians in Keqiao have organized nine blood donation campaigns, involving 754 donations and collecting 278.7 liters of blood. The largest campaign attracted 141 Indian donors. "Since Punhani and his fellow Indians helped Jia Jia at the end of 2014, they have contacted us every year to inform Indian community members about the time and number of participants for their group blood donations," said Jin Danting, an official of Shaoxing Central Blood Station. "They have kept it up for 12 years. Their sincerity and self-lessness have deeply moved us. This kind of love that crosses national borders is truly precious." Jia Jia's father, Wei, said: "I'm grateful to everyone who helped us back then." He said the girl has made a very good recovery. Over the past 12 years, Wei has visited Punhani's company almost every year, sitting down with him to catch up and once again express his gratitude. "Although communication can sometimes be a little difficult, we have overcome the barriers of language and become good friends," Wei said. For Punhani and his fellow Indians, however, donating blood is about more than giving. "When we donate blood and feel that our blood may save someone's life, we feel from the bottom of our hearts that we are doing something for humanity, which has given us so much joy." Many Indian businesspeople have put down roots in Keqiao, home to China Textile City, a major global textile trading hub. Indian businesspeople began arriving in the area in the early 1990s, following historical routes of the Silk Road. Today more than 1,000 Indians live in Keqiao, making them the district's largest foreign business community.

item.title: Africa eyes initiative in disease control
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Africa eyes initiative in disease control Interoperability with existing systems can help enable more timely decisions Health cooperation among BRICS countries could help Africa close persistent gaps in disease surveillance, research, diagnostics and vaccine production while strengthening health systems and improving access to medical products across the Global South, according to experts. The potential benefits are drawing attention as plans advance for a BRICS Integrated Early Warning System for the Prevention and Response to Mass Infectious Diseases. The initiative is aimed at strengthening disease detection, information sharing, preparedness and coordinated responses to future outbreaks. At the 16th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting in Chandigarh, India, in July, member nations supported the establishment of a dedicated sub-working group on the early warning system to advance the initiative, which is considered a milestone in advancing regional and international health security. For Africa, the proposed system could make an important contribution, particularly if it connects effectively with surveillance and early warning systems already in operation across the continent. "In an outbreak, speed matters enormously. The earlier we identify an unusual signal, the greater our chance of containing it before it becomes a much larger emergency," said Saran Koly, director of communication and public information for the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. She said the fast sharing of epidemiological information, laboratory results, genomic data and risk assessments across countries could improve the ability to identify and contain emerging threats. Koly said the priority for Africa should be ensuring interoperability between the BRICS-proposed early warning system and existing continental and national health structures in Africa. "We already have national public-health institutes, laboratory networks, Africa CDC's regional structures and surveillance systems operating across the continent," she said. "The BRICS system will be most useful to us if these systems can communicate with each other and information can move quickly enough to support decisions on the ground." Raphael Obonyo, a Kenyan public policy analyst, said the proposed system could be particularly significant for Africa because it would help establish a common mechanism for tackling diseases and outbreaks, with a focus on prevention, detection and response. He said greater BRICS cooperation could strengthen disease surveillance, diagnostics, vaccine research and manufacturing, as well as technology transfer. "Most importantly, the cooperation will aid Africa in building resilience, innovation and sustainability in the prevention and response to mass infectious diseases," he said. Health is a key area of cooperation among BRICS members, with intensified joint efforts in collaboration in recent years in disease control and prevention, research and innovation and improving universal health coverage. Cooperation mechanisms such as the BRICS Tuberculosis Research Network and BRICS Vaccine Research and Development Centre have been established for member states to collaborate on research, technology transfer and capacity building. Beyond the early warning system, Africa CDC envisions opportunities for other practical cooperation projects between African and BRICS institutions. Several BRICS countries have strong capabilities in pharmaceuticals, vaccines, diagnostics, biotechnology and genomic surveillance. "We would like to see that translated into very practical cooperation with African institutions: joint research, stronger laboratory networks, clinical trials, training, technology transfer, partnerships between manufacturers and faster development of diagnostics and other medical countermeasures," Koly said. For Africa to benefit fully from the emerging cooperation with BRICS in disease prevention and control, Obonyo said institutions such as Africa CDC and national public-health agencies must ensure the necessary systems and capacities are in place to support timely detection and effective responses. African nations must also invest in preparedness before emergencies occur, including through stronger health systems, surveillance and cross-border coordination, he said.

item.title: BRICS pivotal in formulating AI rules
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
BRICS pivotal in formulating AI rules Closing development gap and bridging digital divide are seen as some of its main tasks The BRICS is emerging as a significant force in development and governance of artificial intelligence globally, experts say, highlighting its crucial role in championing the Global South's interests and bridging the digital divide. BRICS has evolved into a crucial mechanism for Global South nations to pursue shared development. With the rise of AI, the bloc has elevated technology governance as a key pillar of its agenda. BRICS members and the broader Global South regard AI as both an unprecedented opportunity and a strategic imperative. Jiang Tianjiao, a research fellow at the Center for Global AI Innovative Governance in Shanghai, said that these countries see developing AI as a way of increasing productivity, improving public services and narrowing the digital divide, but also as an essential path to reduce dependence on developed countries for technology, computing power and rules. A landmark move came at last year's BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where the bloc issued its first leadership-level consensus document on global AI governance, The BRICS Leaders' Statement on the Global Governance of Artificial Intelligence. It underscored digital sovereignty and the right to development as central to global AI governance. The BRICS consensus serves as a crucial corrective to the global AI governance system, experts said. Jiang Qingquan, deputy director of the BRICS Economic Research Center at Xiamen University of Technology, said global AI governance discussions have often fixated on security risks, overlooking the more fundamental issue of the development gap. "By enshrining the right to development as a governance principle, the BRICS statement compels the international community to address the crucial question: how to ensure all countries can access and use AI before discussing its regulation. "BRICS places the right to development at the core of AI governance. Giving priority to capacity building for developing countries better aligns with the practical needs of Global South nations." He depicted the grouping's role as a "collective spokesperson for Global South AI governance". Despite varying strengths in AI technology, computing infrastructure and energy support, experts see these differences as a unique advantage for BRICS multilateral AI collaboration, potentially playing a significant role in bridging the global digital divide. Jiang Tianjiao underscored the complementary strengths among BRICS members in creating a "resources-technology-scenario energy" synergy. "China has a complete AI industrial chain and open-source model capabilities; Russia and India excel in algorithms and talent; Brazil, Indonesia and South Africa have abundant application scenarios in different sectors; and countries such as China and Brazil offer clean energy for high-energy-consuming computing power." This complementarity is translating into concrete mechanisms. In Bengaluru, India, in July, BRICS member nations signed an agreement on collaboration in standardization, the bloc's first collective foray into setting international AI standards. This initiative enables BRICS members to jointly shape international norms within standard-setting bodies, thereby amplifying the voice of emerging economies in frontier technologies governance, Jiang Qingquan said. BRICS is translating consensus into actionable cooperation mechanisms, with China playing a key role in driving this practical implementation, experts said. Addressing the 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan, Russia, in 2024, President Xi Jinping announced the establishment of the China-BRICS Artificial Intelligence Development and Cooperation Center, expressing China's readiness to deepen collaboration on innovation with all BRICS countries to unleash the dividends of AI development. "The center's establishment is about converting this vision into implementable cooperation mechanisms, ensuring BRICS countries become cocreators of innovation in the AI era," said Xu Shan, an expert at the China-BRICS Artificial Intelligence Development and Cooperation Center. The center has facilitated 55 supply-demand matching events for AI companies, promoting plans for international collaboration, she said. Its training programs have reached 105 senior officials in 58 countries, extending the benefits of BRICS collaboration to the wider Global South, she said. For the public at large, Xu said, AI cooperation can translate into tangible improvements: farmers in remote areas using AI-powered pest detection, grassroots hospitals drawing on AI-assisted diagnoses to help alleviate doctor shortages, and speakers of minority languages accessing intelligent services in their native tongues. "The ultimate test of AI collaboration is whether people in BRICS and Global South countries can genuinely benefit from this technological revolution," Xu said. "That is the fundamental purpose of everything the center does."

item.title: Xi: China, India can achieve shared growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Xi: China, India can achieve shared growth Nations urged to provide positive energy for global peace, stability President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that China and India, although having different national conditions, can learn from each other's strengths to achieve shared success and pursue common development. He made the remarks when meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the capital of India. The two leaders had a candid and in-depth exchange of views, reaching an important consensus on China and India being partners. Xi said that amid a complex international situation, China and India — as the two most populous countries and important members of the Global South — bear significant responsibilities. Both countries should keep the future of humanity in mind and the well-being of their peoples at heart, and work together to promote the high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, providing more positive energy for world peace, stability and prosperity, he said. On the development of bilateral relations, Xi urged India to calibrate the direction with an objective and rational strategic understanding, saying that China and India are partners, not rivals, and they represent development opportunities for each other, not threats. Xi underlined the need for both sides to uphold a win-win approach to achieve mutual success. The two countries should expand cooperation in cultural and people-to-people exchanges, as well as increase direct flights, to improve the public opinion foundation of bilateral relations, he said, adding that the two nations should also adopt a balanced approach to address each other's economic and trade concerns. Xi urged eliminating interference with the political wisdom of mutual respect and mutual understanding, saying that the two countries should remain committed to a dual-track approach of advancing bilateral relations and resolving the boundary question, with both reinforcing each other and maintaining peace and tranquility in border areas. He also called for China and India to strengthen coordination within multilateral frameworks in addition to BRICS, such as the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and the Group of 20, and work together to address global challenges and staunchly defend international fairness and justice. During their meeting, Modi assured Xi that India always views its relationship with China from a strategic and long-term perspective. India is willing to be partners with China, rather than rivals, and is ready to view China's development as an opportunity, rather than a challenge, he said. Modi said that India adheres to an independent foreign policy, and its development of relations with China is not influenced by third parties. India's policy and stance on the Taiwan question and issues related to the Xizang autonomous region remain unchanged, and it will not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities in the country, he added. Modi expressed India's readiness to maintain high-level exchanges and strengthen strategic communication with China based on mutual respect and mutual trust, promote mutually beneficial cooperation, and encourage close cultural and people-to-people exchanges to achieve greater development in bilateral relations. He also expressed India's commitment to working with China to maintain peace and tranquility in border areas.

item.title: Xi attends BRICS summit in New Delhi
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
Xi says BRICS world's most influential platform for emerging markets cooperation NEW DELHI -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said here on Saturday that the BRICS cooperation mechanism has become the world's most influential platform for cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries. When addressing the Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Xi noted that this year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation, saying that over the past two decades, the BRICS cooperation mechanism has continued to grow and expand, and has demonstrated remarkable vitality and dynamism. Xi said it has been 20 years of self-reliance and self-strengthening, adding that BRICS countries have actively explored development paths suited to their own national conditions, setting an example of self-strengthening through unity among emerging markets and developing countries. This has also been 20 years of standing together through thick and thin, Xi noted. BRICS countries, Xi said, have worked together to tackle challenges ranging from the global financial crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic to climate change. The group has remained steadfast in safeguarding the common interests of the Global South, while providing the world with stability and positive momentum, he said. Xi also hailed the past 20 years of BRICS cooperation as fruitful, saying that BRICS countries have undergone a historic expansion, established a comprehensive, multi-tiered framework for cooperation, and ushered in a new stage of high-quality development for greater BRICS cooperation. Xi stressed that the world is undergoing accelerated transformation unseen in a century, the Global South is rapidly growing in strength, and the trend toward a multipolar world is unstoppable. Meanwhile, countercurrents of unilateralism and power politics are surging, multilateralism and the international order are coming under strain, and deficits in peace, development, security and governance continue to widen, he added. He said that BRICS countries should firmly stand on the right side of history, strive to be a pioneer of the times, steer the international order toward greater justice and equity, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity. Xi called on BRICS to pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development. BRICS countries, he said, should firmly seize the initiative, strengthen cooperation in artificial intelligence, encourage open-source development, openness, cooperation and sharing, and push practical cooperation into new areas and to new heights. BRICS countries are welcome to actively participate in the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, he said. China proposed an initiative to promote new industrialization through artificial intelligence among BRICS countries, and is willing to work with all parties to deliver more outcomes in research, development and application, and deepen cooperation in industrial and supply chains, he said. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in upholding peace and stability. BRICS countries should uphold a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, oppose the Cold War mentality and bloc confrontation, reject violations of other countries' sovereignty and interference in their internal affairs, and play a constructive role in resolving hotspot issues, making a distinctive BRICS contribution to finding solutions that address both symptoms and root causes, he said. Noting that the situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid, Xi said this war has inflicted serious losses on the people of all countries in the region, and it is against the common interests of the international community. Xi said he has set out four propositions on safeguarding and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East, which are aimed at de-escalation, ending hostilities and promoting peace. Xi urged relevant parties to keep to the direction of political settlement, and work for a permanent, comprehensive ceasefire. China will work with fellow BRICS members to play a due role in bringing peace and tranquility to the Middle East, he said. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in facilitating mutual learning between civilizations. The countries, he said, should champion the common values of humanity and advocate exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations as well as harmonious coexistence. They should ensure the success of the BRICS forum on people-to-people and cultural exchanges, share experience in state governance, and build positive momentum for the steady development of relations between countries, Xi added. Xi advocated efforts to deepen cooperation in culture, tourism and education, strengthen youth exchanges, and promote more frequent interactions and closer bonds among the peoples. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in reforming and improving global governance. He urged the group to keep pace with the trend toward greater democracy in international relations, promote a more just and equitable global governance system, and uphold the authority of the United Nations. Xi said BRICS should support a multilateral trading system centered on the World Trade Organization, and reject all forms of protectionist measures. The grouping should lead global governance in emerging domains such as cyberspace, outer space and the deep sea, and amplify the voice of Global South countries, he added. Over an extraordinary two-decade journey, solidarity and cooperation have remained the driving force behind the BRICS cause, Xi stressed. Xi called on BRICS members to remain sincere and candid with one another, seek common ground while respecting differences, and respect each other's core concerns. He also urged the group to deepen mutual understanding through communication and dialogue, properly handle differences, and ensure that BRICS cooperation continues to move forward steadily. China, Xi said, will take over as the rotating chair of the BRICS and host the 19th summit next year. The Chinese side stands ready to work with all parties to build consensus, create a better future, and embark on BRICS' third "golden decade," jointly opening up a bright future of prosperity and progress, he added. At the summit, all parties spoke highly of the development achievements made by BRICS over the past 20 years, noting that the BRICS mechanism has broad representation and great potential for development. In the face of escalating geopolitical conflicts and the rise of unilateralism, BRICS countries have a responsibility to speak up for the Global South, uphold multilateralism, support the central role of the United Nations, uphold the sovereign equality of all countries, abide by international law, oppose interference in the internal affairs of other countries, support free trade, and jointly address global challenges, they said. All parties should uphold the BRICS spirit, deepen cooperation across various fields, enhance economic resilience, promote a more just and inclusive international order, and build a secure and prosperous multipolar world, they added. All parties appreciated China's important contribution to the development and expansion of the BRICS mechanism and supported China, as next year's BRICS chair, in successfully hosting the 19th BRICS Summit, so as to jointly bring BRICS cooperation to a new level. The leaders also adopted a joint declaration at the summit.
